enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: A SAML Source can be configured to allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation explicitly warns that this may constitute a security risk because the request is not verified.
saml.note: Do not report acceptance of unsolicited SAML responses as a bug when this mode is intentionally enabled.

saml.description: SAML sources can optionally allow IdP-initiated logins, which accept unsolicited assertions without prior SP interaction.
saml.note: This weakens request-binding guarantees by configuration; acceptance of unsolicited assertions is not necessarily a bug if this option was enabled.

saml.description: When a Source stage suspends a flow and the configured resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning.
saml.note: A restarted flow after timeout is by design and should not be flagged as flow-coherence failure.

saml.description: If a source's authentication or enrollment flow contains a User Login stage, the Source stage will directly authenticate the pending user instead of resuming the original flow.
saml.note: This can look like session confusion but is documented behavior caused by unsupported flow composition.

saml.description: Policies bound to flow-stage bindings may be evaluated either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run, producing context-dependent differences by design.
saml.note: Different outcomes before and after user identification can be expected when stage-run evaluation is enabled.

saml.description: Applications with no policy/group/user bindings are accessible to all users by default.
saml.note: Broad access in an unbound application is by design and should not be treated as authorization escalation.

saml.description: When an OAuth/OIDC client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested.
saml.note: Extra claims in UserInfo or tokens may be expected unless the test explicitly requests a narrower scope set.

saml.description: In releases prior to 2025.10, the email scope always set email_verified to True; as of 2025.10 it defaults to False.
saml.note: Tests that rely on email_verified must account for version-specific default behavior.

saml.description: Transient SAML NameID is based on the user's session ID and is not stable across sessions.
saml.source: SAML Provider docs, Default NameID policy table.
saml.note: Different granted identifiers for the same user across sessions are expected with transient NameID.

saml.description: Persistent SAML NameID is set to the user's hashed ID rather than a human-readable username or email.
saml.source: SAML Provider docs, Default NameID policy table.
saml.note: A hashed downstream identifier is expected and should not be flagged as identity corruption.

saml.description: Identification stage can intentionally accept arbitrary user identifiers and continue the flow even when the user does not exist.
saml.note: This is anti-enumeration behavior and can resemble identity confusion if the test assumes early rejection of unknown users.

saml.constraint: For SAML I1 tests against authentik as SP, use the SAML Source ACS endpoint /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ with SP-initiated flow initialization. The executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first so the forged SAMLResponse carries a matching InResponseTo; otherwise authentik will reject the response for flow/state reasons rather than signature or issuer validation.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins on a SAML Source is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For default-config I1/I3 testing, the fuzzer MUST distinguish acceptance caused by enabling IDP-initiated logins from acceptance of an SP-initiated forged response. Do NOT enable IDP-initiated logins unless the test specifically targets that insecure mode.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution and related signature tests, authentik documentation states the SAML Source supports signed requests, but the provided docs do not expose a per-request toggle or API field for disabling signature validation. The fuzzer MUST treat successful forged-login results as meaningful only when using a source configuration intended to validate signatures; otherwise a false positive may reflect insecure source setup rather than proof-processing logic.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML Source with a concrete upstream Issuer/Entity ID and then send a mismatched assertion Issuer. If the source is created without a fixed upstream issuer expectation, an issuer-mismatch test can become inconclusive because there is no configured trust anchor to compare against.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), include a CONTROL login using a valid SAMLResponse on the same source before the attack login. Without a control, rejection of the attack response cannot be distinguished from broken source configuration, missing flow state, or generic ACS failure.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, set NotOnOrAfter in the past only after confirming the same source accepts a normal assertion. authentik acts as SP at /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ and consumes assertions at the ACS URL; failures can also arise from flow/session mismatch, so a control is mandatory.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage resume, note that Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later, but only until the configured Resume timeout. If the timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning. The fuzzer MUST keep multi-step SAML source tests within the resume timeout or else a restart is by design, not a coherence violation.

For I3 tests that embed a SAML Source inside another flow via Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. Documentation states that if a User Login stage is bound, the source flow authenticates directly instead of resuming the original flow. A test that observes non-resumption in that configuration is a setup error, not a vulnerability.

For I3 config-change tests on flows and policies, authentik can evaluate stage-bound policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. The fuzzer MUST account for this documented behavior: a change observed only across separate flow executions may be by design. A valid same-flow coherence test must show inconsistent handling within one execution, not merely after replanning.

For I3 tests involving direct flow denial or conditional stages, Deny-stage behavior depends on stage-binding evaluation timing. Documentation explicitly warns that effective deny behavior requires 'Evaluate when flow is planned' disabled. The fuzzer MUST not interpret stage-skipping or denial differences as security bugs unless binding evaluation mode is controlled.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, NameID is the primary identifier in SAML assertions, but authentik documentation also warns that Email-address NameID is mutable and not recommended as a persistent identifier. The fuzzer SHOULD test both persistent NameID and email-based NameID separately and MUST NOT treat email-based account linking/merging behavior as equivalent to persistent-ID binding.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, if the SAML Source NameID Policy is set to Email address, collisions with existing accounts may reflect administrator choice of a mutable identifier. The fuzzer MUST record the configured NameID policy and distinguish insecure auto-linking from by-design email-based identity selection.

For I4 tests involving multiple upstream identities, do not assume wildcard matching semantics for SAML identifiers because the provided authentik SAML docs do not document any wildcard/regex matching mode for NameID or issuer constraints on SAML Source configuration. Treat configured identifier comparisons as exact unless separately documented; if multiple distinct identities must authenticate through the same source, omit exact-binding fields rather than using '*' as a wildcard.

For I5 saml_no_conditions and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, authentik as SP consumes assertions at the ACS URL, and the docs describe ACS validation responsibilities in general SAML terms (issuer, audience, time conditions). The fuzzer MUST test missing Conditions and wrong Audience separately: acceptance without Conditions indicates missing temporal/audience enforcement, while wrong Audience with Conditions present isolates audience validation.

For I5 authorization tests that rely on OAuth/OIDC tokens after SAML login, remember that UserInfo only returns claims allowed by requested/configured scopes. In authentik, when no scopes are requested, all configured scopes are treated as requested. The fuzzer MUST control requested scopes during token-based verification to avoid false positives where extra claims are present by default scope behavior rather than over-grant by SAML mapping.

For I5 tests using email_verified after SAML or other federated login, authentik documentation states that as of 2025.10 the email scope defaults email_verified to False, while prior releases always set it to True. The fuzzer MUST version-gate any unverified-email-account-linking or authorization conclusions based on email_verified, because older versions may assert True by design.

SAML Source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I1 default-config testing, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated ACS testing from intentionally enabled IdP-initiated mode; acceptance in IdP-initiated mode is not evidence of missing request binding.

For SAML I1 tests against authentik as SP, the executor MUST use SP-initiated flow setup before posting to /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ because authentik expects request-bound flow state. The SAML login operation therefore requires initiate_saml_flow=true so the fabricated SAMLResponse can carry the matching InResponseTo.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a CONTROL SAML login without expired_assertion first. Otherwise a failed expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken source/provider setup or flow misconfiguration.

For I2 replay tests, authentik documentation only explicitly states expiry checking for externally issued JWTs in machine-to-machine mode ('exp attribute is not set as now or in the past'). The docs provided do not explicitly document SAML assertion ID replay or OneTimeUse enforcement behavior. The fuzzer SHOULD treat replay acceptance as a test result, but MUST use the exact same Assertion ID across attempts when testing replay semantics.

SAML source configuration includes a NameID Policy selector. Different upstream NameID formats can map to different local identifiers (persistent hashed ID, distinguishedName, UPN, transient session ID, email address). For I4 identity-collision tests, the fuzzer MUST keep NameID policy constant across compared logins; changing NameID format changes the identifier source and can create false positives.

Email-based NameID is documented as unsafe because users are free to change email addresses by default. For I4/I5 tests involving account linking or principal binding, any identity merge based on email-address NameID may be by configuration choice rather than parser confusion. Record when email-address NameID policy is in use and do not compare it directly to persistent/transient NameID behavior.

Transient NameID is documented as being based on the user's session ID. For I4 principal-binding tests, transient NameID MUST NOT be used as the stable sent identity because the same user can receive different identifiers across sessions by design.

Persistent NameID is documented as the user's hashed ID. For I4 verification, the granted identifier may be a stable hashed value rather than the raw upstream username/email. Do not flag this transformation as a collision unless two distinct upstream principals map to the same downstream identity.

SAML source 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' default false should remain false for request-coherence and unsolicited-response testing. Enabling it broadens acceptance semantics and can mask failures in SP request correlation (I3) or issuer/request validation (I1).

Source stage resume behavior is time-bound by 'Resume timeout'. For any multi-step flow that embeds a SAML source through a Source stage, if the timeout is exceeded the suspended flow restarts from the beginning. For I3 flow-coherence tests, apparent loss of session binding after long delays may be by design due to resume timeout expiry, not a coherence bug.

Flow-stage policy evaluation mode affects when access decisions are computed. If a stage binding is configured with 'Evaluate when flow is planned', decisions can be made before later user-identifying input exists. For I3 tests involving mid-flow identity-dependent policy changes, the fuzzer MUST account for whether policies are evaluated at planning time or stage-run time; otherwise inconsistent results may be by design.

Application access defaults are permissive when no bindings are defined: all users can access applications if no bindings are attached. For I5 authorization-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST explicitly configure restrictive bindings/policies before expecting denial; otherwise broad access is documented default behavior, not an escalation.

OAuth/OIDC scope behavior is permissive by default: when a client requests no scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. For any verification using /application/o/userinfo/ or token claims, the fuzzer MUST request explicit minimal scopes in control and attack cases; omitting scope can over-grant claims by design and create false I5 positives.

Refresh tokens are only issued when both the application and authentik are configured for offline_access and the request includes offline_access. Tests that assume refresh-token issuance or revocation MUST include offline_access explicitly; absence of a refresh token is otherwise by design.

The OAuth token endpoint /application/o/token/ is shared across grant types. For password-based admin bootstrap in SAML profiles, authentik documents client_credentials and password-style submissions on this endpoint. The fuzzer MUST send application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies, not JSON.

The UserInfo endpoint returns standardized claims about the authenticated user when called with a valid access token. The fuzzer MUST use the access_token as session_token for verify_granted_identity, never an id_token.

Token introspection in authentik is provider-scoped: you can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless you first exchange it for a token from that provider. For I5 cross-provider token tests, introspection failure across providers is expected and not itself evidence of audience enforcement.

For OIDC/SAML single logout related tests, back-channel logout is the only documented mechanism guaranteed to run on administrative session termination. Front-channel behavior depends on browser interaction and provider support. Do not treat missing front-channel logout after admin session deletion as a vulnerability when back-channel is not configured.

SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is security-relevant. For SP-request-bound tests (I1/I3/I5), the fuzzer MUST keep IdP-initiated logins disabled so authentik requires an SP-initiated flow and request context. Enabling it permits unsolicited assertions and can make request-binding tests pass or fail for the wrong reason.

For all SAML ACS tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo context. authentik documents the ACS at /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ and SAML flows are SP-initiated unless IdP-initiated logins are explicitly allowed. Sending a fabricated POST without first initiating the flow will be rejected for flow-state reasons, not necessarily because the security check worked.

For I1 signature-validation default tests, if the SAML source is configured with signed requests support but the docs do not expose a per-request signature-validation toggle here, the fuzzer MUST treat acceptance/rejection as dependent on source configuration rather than assume signatures are always enforced. Use a control login with a valid SAML flow before concluding that attacker-signed assertions were accepted or rejected due to signature handling.

For I1 issuer-mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with an explicit IdP Issuer/Entity ID and then send a mismatched Issuer. If the source is left loosely configured, a successful login may reflect missing issuer pinning in setup rather than a runtime bypass. The fuzzer MUST include a control login using the expected issuer first.

The SAML source's NameID Policy controls how upstream identities are interpreted. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins. Changing between Persistent, EmailAddress, Windows, or other NameID formats changes the identifier semantics and can create false collision or non-collision results.

Email-based NameID is documented as mutable and not recommended as a stable identifier. For I4 collision/account-linking tests, the fuzzer SHOULD prefer Persistent NameID over EmailAddress when testing stable principal binding. If EmailAddress NameID is used, identity merges based on changed email are not reliable evidence of a broker flaw without additional controls.

For I4 email-binding collision tests against authentik as SP, the fuzzer MUST vary NameID and email independently and verify which attribute authentik binds on. The docs distinguish NameID as the unique identifier in the assertion, while property mappings can also carry email and username attributes. A collision based on email may be by configuration/account-linking behavior rather than NameID confusion unless the source mapping is controlled.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid assertion first. Otherwise, a failed attack login cannot be distinguished from broken source configuration, missing flow state, or generic ACS rejection.

For I2 replay tests, authentik documents SAML session tracking for providers and flow resumption timeouts for source-stage embedding, but these are not substitutes for assertion replay detection. The fuzzer MUST reuse the same Assertion ID across two ACS submissions in the same source configuration and compare outcomes directly; do not infer replay protection from session logout behavior or flow timeout behavior.

Source Stage has a 'Resume timeout' after which the suspended flow restarts from the beginning. For I3 multi-step coherence tests involving embedded SAML/OAuth sources, the fuzzer MUST complete the external authentication and return before this timeout expires. Otherwise, flow restart is by design and must not be reported as session confusion or broken atomicity.

When testing SAML via a Source Stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. authentik explicitly states this causes the source flow to authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow. If present, apparent MFA bypass or flow-skip behavior is a setup artifact, not an I3 vulnerability.

Flow-stage policy timing matters for I3 tests. authentik can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test MUST keep this setting fixed and interpret differences accordingly; re-evaluation at stage-run time can legitimately change behavior based on newly available context and is not itself a race-condition bug.

If the Identification stage has 'Pretend user exists' enabled, nonexistent identifiers are intentionally allowed to proceed to later stages. For I4 and account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST disable this option or account for it, otherwise downstream behavior may look like identity confusion when it is actually anti-enumeration behavior by design.

For SAML-source tests that rely on source buttons in the Identification stage, note that when no user fields are selected and only one source is selected, authentik automatically redirects to that source. The fuzzer MUST account for this auto-redirect behavior when reasoning about flow steps and session binding; missing an intermediate page is by design, not a flow-skip bug.

UserInfo verification uses the OAuth access token, not the SAML assertion. In SAML-source scenarios, verify_granted_identity reflects the post-broker session claims after authentik login. The fuzzer MUST not treat absence of raw SAML fields in /application/o/userinfo/ as evidence that claims were dropped unless corresponding scope/property mappings were configured to expose them.

When no OAuth scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested. For I5 authorization-binding tests that use UserInfo after SAML login, the fuzzer MUST explicitly request a minimal scope set; omitting scope can broaden returned claims by design and create false-positive over-grant findings.

Email scope behavior changed in authentik 2025.10: email_verified now defaults to false, whereas prior releases always set it to true. For I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST record the authentik version and not treat email_verified=true on older versions as proof of verified email handling; it is documented legacy behavior.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
